subject: Tailwind Robotics — memory variant analysis & quantization effects for Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Ethan Wallace <ethan@tailwind.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@tailwind.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — model variants, long context & quantization impact

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me for a sizing packet to start internal approvals. High level: we'll be running three variants in production — a tuned 13B (chat-heavy), a 30B fine-tuned for retrieval-augmented generation, and a 70B for high-fidelity hallucination-sensitive tasks. Typical usage profile: 6k–32k context windows (we expect many requests at ~8k, some at 32k), and peak concurrent sessions of ~30. We want to understand:

- realistic GPU footprint per model variant (including KV cache for the different context lengths)
- how using 8-bit and 4-bit quantization changes GPU counts and whether we can meet latency SLOs (p95 < 600ms for chat-sized requests)
- recommended reserved pool (and buffer) for an initial commit — Tailwind is open to a 12–18 month reserved contract if the numbers make sense

Can you put together a short spreadsheet and a one-page summary for procurement? I already uploaded our expected QPS sample into the Drive link (see attached).

Also, is Redwood able to automatically route requests to a lower-precision variant when capacity is constrained? That would help headroom planning.

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Wallace
Head of ML Platforms, Tailwind Robotics

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — model variants, long context & quantization impact

Ethan —

Thanks — pulling together the workbook now. Below is our concise sizing summary and assumptions so procurement can get a quick read. I'll attach the workbook with per‑replica counts and an autoscaling policy suggestion.

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Peak concurrent sessions: 30 (you listed 30; workbook uses 40 as a safety buffer)
- Average request length: 1k tokens; worst-case up to 8k; some sessions use 32k for long docs
- Target p95 latency: <= 600ms for chat-sized (~1k token) requests under committed capacity
- GPUs available for Dedicated: 80GB (H100/A100 NVL) or 48GB (A100 40GB w/ NVLink pooling)

Quick memory & KV cache model (rounded):
- 13B (tuned chat model): base fp16 resident ~28 GB; int8 ~14 GB; int4 ~10 GB.
  KV cache for 8k context ~2.5 GB; for 32k context ~10 GB.
  Effective single‑replica footprint (13B + 32k): fp16 ~38 GB; int8 ~24 GB; int4 ~20 GB.
  Recommended GPU: single 40GB/48GB for int8/int4 variants; 80GB for fp16 32k if avoiding quantization.

- 30B (fine‑tuned RAG): base fp16 ~60 GB; int8 ~30 GB; int4 ~20 GB.
  KV cache for 8k ~5.5 GB; for 32k ~22 GB.
  Effective footprint (30B + 32k): fp16 ~82 GB; int8 ~52 GB; int4 ~42 GB.
  Recommended GPU: 80GB class for fp16 (single replica); int8 can fit in 48–80GB with headroom; int4 fits readily on 48GB.

- 70B (high-fidelity): base fp16 ~140 GB; int8 ~70 GB; int4 ~40 GB (aggressive QAT/LLM.int4).
  KV cache for 8k ~13 GB; for 32k ~52 GB.
  Effective footprint (70B + 32k): fp16 ~192 GB; int8 ~122 GB; int4 ~92 GB.
  Recommended approach: model-split across 2x80GB GPUs for int8, or 3+ shard configuration for fp16. Using int4 can make single 80GB replicas feasible with model parallelism optimizations and KV offload to host/SSD for rarely accessed tokens.

Sizing notes and fleet recommendation (initial commit — conservative):
- Baseline reserved pool: 8x 80GB GPUs (H100/A100-NVL class). This supports:
  - 13B: 6 replicas (int8/int4) for throughput + failover
  - 30B: 4 replicas (mix int8 primary, fp16 fallback)
  - 70B: sharded replicas across 4 GPU nodes (2x 80GB per logical replica) for low‑latency path; recommend 2 logical replicas reserved (i.e., ~4 physical GPUs)
- Buffer: +20% headroom to absorb QPS spikes and background maintenance.
- Autoscaling: allow burst pool (shared hosted or pre-emptible) up to an additional 12 GPUs for traffic spikes; configure automatic fallback to int8/int4 variants when committed capacity is saturated.
- KV cache optimizations: enable prefix caching for common prompts and aggressive KV eviction policy for long-tail 32k sessions; recommend deduplication + short-lived cache TTLs (1–5 minutes) to reduce memory pressure.

Tradeoffs and latency expectations:
- Quantizing 30B -> int8 reduces per-replica footprint ~2x and generally preserves top‑line quality; p95 latency improves 15–30% because more requests fit on a single GPU and batching is more efficient.
- 70B in int8/int4 is feasible but requires careful model sharding and validation. For latency-sensitive paths we recommend keeping a fp16 fallback replica (or HPS offload patterns) for the highest-stakes calls.

I'll attach the workbook with per‑model replica counts mapped to your QPS sample, plus cost estimates for reserved vs burst capacity. If Tailwind confirms the workload distribution (percent of traffic to each model + % of 32k requests), we can finalize committed GPU counts and a SLA exhibit for procurement.

Next steps:
1) I'll upload the workbook and the one‑pager to Drive by EOD.
2) Marissa will run a quick perf sweep on 70B int8 to validate the ~92 GB int4 projection (cc'd).
3) Dev will propose an autoscale policy that prioritizes routing to quantized variants under saturation.

Would you like a short 30‑minute follow-up with procurement and your infra lead?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.inference.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — memory variant analysis & quantization effects for Dedicated pool

Ethan, Jonas — quick note from our perf run: we ran synthetic passes on the 70B int8 shim and saw steady-state p95 for 1k tokens in ~480ms on a dual-H100 (80GB) split config using our optimized kernels and KV prefetch. For 32k contexts we saw a tail increase — p95 ~1.2s — driven by KV marshaling.

Practical recommendation:
- For Tailwind's latency SLOs, keep 13B and 30B as primary int8 replicas.
- For 70B, reserve 2 logical replicas on 2x80GB each (so 4 physical 80GB GPUs) and enable a cold fp16 fallback (single logical replica) for edge cases or degraded QoS.

I'll update the workbook with the measured latency rows and include a note on KV offload settings we used (async host offload for >24k tokens).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
